question.leadin: This leader edited the Ems Dispatch, helping to start a war with France.
question.text: Name this man whose use of Realpolitik earned him the nickname the "Iron Chancellor."
question.clue: This man edited the Ems Dispatch to provoke the Franco-Prussian War.

swap.leadin: This group was opposed by an organization called the Lizard League. which has nothing to do with any insane modern conspiracy theories.
swap.text: Name this Christian order of crusading knights, who converted the Baltic countries to Christianity. They were defeated by the forces of Wladyslaw II Jagiello (vwah-DEE-swahf "the second" yah-GYEH-woh) at the Battle of Grunwald.
swap.answerHtml: Teutonic Order [or the Teutonic Knights, or the Order of Brothers of the German House of Saint Mary in Jerusalem]
swap.clue: A force from this group fought at the Battle of Legnica against the Mongols.

question.text: In 1961, the East and West halves of the East German capital were separated by this structure, which could be crossed at Checkpoint Charlie.
question.clue: The construction of this object created "ghost stations" in which subways on certain lines would not stop.

swap.leadin: This country's majority political parties, the Christian Democratic Union and Christian Social Union, opposed a vote on same-sex marriage until 2017, when its chancellor put the issue to a conscience vote.
swap.text: Name this European country where, in June 2017, the Bundestag voted to legalize same-sex marriage.
swap.clue: Following World War I, the Weimar ("VIE-mar") Republic was established in this nation.

question.text: Swiss banks notoriously stored gold from the plunder of this government's occupied territories. The Bergier Commission investigated Switzerland's involvement in the auctions of "degenerate art" rebuked by this government.
question.answerHtml: Nazi Germany [or the Third Reich; prompt on Germany; prompt on the Reich]
question.clue: Opposed by the White Rose student group, this government held the Wannsee Conference and constructed a no speed-limit highway called the autobahn.

swap.text: Charles V (the fifth) summoned Luther to this imperial diet (dye-it) in 1521 to respond to Leo X's (the tenth's)Exsurge Domine(ayk-SUR-jay DOH-mee-nay). Luther was declared a "notorious heretic" after this diet.
swap.clue: One prominent participant in this meeting had to hide at the Wartburg at its conclusion.

question.leadin: Otto von Bismarck eerily predicted that in the same way "[The Battle of Jena] came twenty years after [this leader's] death, the crash" would come twenty years after him.
question.text: Name this "enlightened despot" who defeated Maria Theresa's troops to annex Silesia.
question.answerHtml: Frederick the Great [or Frederick II; prompt on Frederick] (Prophetically, Germany‘s Spring Offensive in World War I failed only 7 days after the 20 year anniversary of Bismark’s departure)
question.clue: Following the capture of Dresden's mints, this ruler created debased Polish money, earning the kingdom some 25 million taler.

swap.text: This German used Gutenberg's press to distribute his Ninety-Five Theses and attack indulgences, triggering the Protestant Reformation and the Iconoclastic Riots later on.
swap.clue: Those pitfalls may have caused him to write such pamphlets as Against the Heavenly Prophets and Against the Jews and Their Lies.

question.text: John George I ("the first"), the ruler of this state, was forced to ally with Gustavus Adolphus after his lands were invaded by Tilly shortly before Breitenfeld.
question.clue: During World War I, George V renamed a royal house named for this region, Coburg, and Gotha to the House of Windsor.

swap.leadin: It relied heavily on the Formicarius of Johannes Nider, and most published versions included a forward containing the bull Summis desiderantes affectibus.
swap.text: Identify this work of Heinrich Kramer and James Sprenger.
swap.answerHtml: The Malleus Maleficarum [or Der Hexenhammer; or The Witches Hammer; or The Hammer Against Witches]
swap.clue: Its first part delineates a certain heresy, while its second part contains a compendium of fabulous stories.

question.text: The Munich Agreement allowed the annexation by Nazi Germany of this region of Czechoslovakia historically inhabited by German speakers.
question.clue: This majority German-speaking territory that was handed over in the Munich Pact, a cession that Neville Chamberlain claimed had brought "peace for our time."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a school.
swap.text: Established in 1919, this school of design moved to in 1926, and closed because of Nazi hostility in 1933.

question.text: During the battle, 84 members of the 285th Field Artillery Observation Battalion were murdered during the Malmedy Massacre by troops commanded by this Waffen-SS officer.

swap.text: Not coincidentally, in the same year, Russia passed this repressive set of laws to restrict Jewish settlement in the Pale and forbid Jews from engaging in business on Sundays.
swap.clue: One group of laws with this name began a wave of attacks starting in Elizabetgrad and followed from an interpretation of an averted railway accident by Konstantin Pobedonostev.

question.text: This Jewish businessman and Weimar-era statesman negotiated the Treaty of Rapallo with the Soviet Union. He was assassinated by the right-wing Operation Consul, after which he was seen as a democratic martyr.
question.clue: The assassins of this German Jewish industrialist and politician may have thought he was an Elder of Zion. This man served as foreign secretary in the Weimar Republic, in which capacity he negotiated the Treaty of Rapallo.

swap.text: The winter of 1917, the worst period of starvation during the blockade, was commonly given this name in Germany. This name refers to the foodstuff Germans were forced to eat after almost every other crop failed.

question.leadin: Its first ruler was Otto of Scheyern, who in 1124 moved his family to their namesake castle on the Paar.
question.text: Name this German noble house, which ruled Bavaria from 1180 until 1918.
question.clue: Joseph II seized on the 1778 death of a member of this house to occupy their territory, only to be forced to withdraw by Frederick the Great in the Treaty of Teschen.

swap.leadin: These people, who claimed that they had received messages from the Holy Spirit, were among those labeled as Fanatics by Martin Luther.
swap.text: Give this collective name for three religious agitators whose names were probably Nicholas Storch, Thomas Dreschel, and Marcus Stubner.
swap.clue: Luther also opposed this group of Anabaptists influenced by Thomas Muntzer. This group, which included Thomas Dreschal and Nicholas Storch, believed themselves to receive messages directly from God.

question.leadin: A distinguished soldier from Magdeburg, this figure fought alongside Major von Muhlenfels at a battle fought nearby Hamakari.
question.text: Identify this military figure responsible for much the genocide that killed civilians and soldier alike at the Battle of Waterburg.
question.clue: The Herero Genocide was largely the handiwork of this German commander, who drove the Herero into the desert after the Battle of Waterberg, poisoned their water, and encircled the desert with his soldiers so that they could not escape.

swap.leadin: Their 1819 passage was sparked by the murder of August von Kotzebue by a student.
swap.text: Name these series of laws that placed government agents in all universities, put all newspapers under government supervision, and expelled overly liberal teachers and students.
swap.clue: Burschenschaften fraternities were banned by these laws, which created an investigatory committee in Mainz to investigate "revolutionary activities" in the German states and gave the Diet censorship powers.
